rt2: light cleaning

Code 
# ============================================== #
# simple cleaning

# glimpse(rt)
# glimpse(rt2)


cols_upper <- c("recorder_name",
                "reference_no",
                "study_area",
                "specific_area",
                "taxonomic_unit",
                "taxonomic_unit_revised",
                "kingdom",
                "phylum",
                "class",
                "order",
                "family",
                "genus")



rt2 <- rt %>% 
  # convert space in columns to underbar
  rename_with(~ .x %>%
                str_replace_all(" ", "_") %>%
                str_to_lower()) %>% 
  
  # convert text to lower (except specified columns)
  mutate(across(c(where(is.character),
                  -all_of(cols_upper)),
                str_to_lower)) %>% 
  
  # replace NA with "na"
  mutate(across(everything(),
                ~ tidyr::replace_na(.x, "na"))) %>% 
  # taxonomy
  relocate(kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, 
           .after = taxonomic_unit_revised)

# glimpse(rt2)

rt3: light cleaning

Code 
# ============================================== #
# filter out irrelevant data at initial stage
# edit start period and end period data

rt2$include %>% unique() %>% sort()
[1] 0 1 2
Code 
rt3 <- rt2 %>% 
  filter(
    # this include col was made in excel for rows based on:
    # n_years: too large (comparison with glacial time)
    # gradient = na
    # magnitude_of_shift = na
    # notes = no resurvey
    # include == 2 is "pending" literature
    include %in% 1) %>%
  
  # start period
  rename(startperiod_orig = start_period) %>%
  mutate(
    # extract all 4-digit years
    startperiod_years = str_extract_all(startperiod_orig, "\\d{4}"),
    
    startperiod_startyear = map_int(
      startperiod_years,
      ~ ifelse(length(.x) == 0, NA_integer_, as.integer(.x[1]))
    ),
    
    startperiod_endyear = map_int(
      startperiod_years,
      ~ ifelse(length(.x) == 0, NA_integer_, as.integer(.x[length(.x)]))
    ),
    
    startperiod_midyear = (startperiod_startyear + startperiod_endyear) / 2
  ) %>%
  select(-startperiod_years) %>% 
  relocate(startperiod_startyear, startperiod_endyear, startperiod_midyear, .after = startperiod_orig) %>% 
  
  # end period
  rename(endperiod_orig = end_period) %>%
  mutate(
    # extract all 4-digit years
    endperiod_years = str_extract_all(endperiod_orig, "\\d{4}"),
    
    endperiod_startyear = map_int(
      endperiod_years,
      ~ ifelse(length(.x) == 0, NA_integer_, as.integer(.x[1]))
    ),
    
    endperiod_endyear = map_int(
      endperiod_years,
      ~ ifelse(length(.x) == 0, NA_integer_, as.integer(.x[length(.x)]))
    ),
    
    endperiod_midyear = (endperiod_startyear + endperiod_endyear) / 2
  ) %>%
  select(-endperiod_years) %>% 
  relocate(endperiod_startyear, endperiod_endyear, endperiod_midyear, .after = endperiod_orig) %>% 
  
  # n_years
  mutate(
    n_years_midyear = endperiod_midyear - startperiod_midyear
  ) %>% 
  relocate(n_years_midyear, .after = n_years) %>% 
  mutate(
  azimuth_of_shift = na_if(azimuth_of_shift, "na"),
  azimuth_of_shift = as.numeric(azimuth_of_shift)
)

  filter(reference_no %in% unique(rt3$reference_no)) %>% 
  select(reference_no, article_title, data_section, source_title, publication_year, authors, doi) %>% 
  mutate(publication_year = as.numeric(publication_year),
         language = "English")

  filter(reference_no %in% unique(rt3$reference_no)) %>% 
  select(reference_no, article_title, data_section, source_title, publication_year, authors, doi) %>% 
  mutate(language = "Japanese")

# ------------ #
# conversion from latitude degrees to km
latdeg_to_km <- function(deg) {
  earth_radius <- 6371
  deg * 2 * pi * earth_radius / 360
}

# ---- #
# example 

latdeg_to_km(0.1)
[1] 11.11949
Code 
# ---- #



# ------------ #
# conversion from longitude degrees to km
londeg_to_km <- function(deg, latitude) {
  earth_radius <- 6371
  deg * 2 * pi * earth_radius / 360 * cos(latitude * pi / 180)
}

# ---- #
# example

londeg_to_km(1, latitude = 36)
[1] 89.95859
Code 
londeg_to_km(1, latitude = 46)
[1] 77.24249
Code 
# ---- #

# lat mean for longitude studies
lon_latrange2 <- lon_latrange %>% 
  rename_with(~ .x %>%
                str_replace_all(" ", "_") %>%
                str_to_lower()) %>% 
  # convert text to lower (except specified columns)
  mutate(gradient = str_to_lower(gradient)) %>% 
  filter(include == 1) %>% 
  rowwise() %>% 
  mutate(lat_mean = mean(lat_min, lat_max)) %>% 
  select(reference_no, gradient, lat_mean)
  






# ------------ #
rt5 <- rt4 %>% 
  
  left_join(lon_latrange2, 
            by = c("reference_no", "gradient")) %>% 
  
  # transform magnitudeshift and unitshift
  mutate(
    
    magnitude_of_shift = case_when(
      
      # apply these to magnitudeshift depending on
      # gradient
      # unitshift
      
      
      # ------------------------------------------------------
      # elevation --> m/year
      # ------------------------------------------------------
      
      # m --> m/year
      gradient == "elevation" & unit_of_shift == "m" ~
        magnitude_of_shift / n_years_midyear,
      
      
      # ------------------------------------------------------
      # latitude --> km/year
      # ------------------------------------------------------
      
      # degree --> km --> km/year
      gradient == "latitude" & unit_of_shift == "degree" ~
        latdeg_to_km(magnitude_of_shift) / n_years_midyear,
      
      # degree/year --> km/year
      gradient == "latitude" & unit_of_shift == "degree/year" ~
        latdeg_to_km(magnitude_of_shift),
      
      # km --> km/year
      gradient == "latitude" & unit_of_shift == "km" ~
        magnitude_of_shift / n_years_midyear,
      
      # already km/year
      gradient == "latitude" & unit_of_shift == "km/year" ~
        magnitude_of_shift,
      
      
      # ------------------------------------------------------
      # longitude --> km/year
      # ------------------------------------------------------
      
      # degree --> km --> km/year
      gradient == "longitude" & unit_of_shift == "degree" ~
        londeg_to_km(magnitude_of_shift, latitude = lat_mean) / n_years_midyear,
      
      # degree/year --> km/year
      gradient == "longitude" & unit_of_shift == "degree/year" ~
        londeg_to_km(magnitude_of_shift, latitude = lat_mean),
      
      
      
      # ------------------------------------------------------
      # horizontal --> km/year
      # ------------------------------------------------------
      
      # km --> km/year
      gradient == "horizontal" & unit_of_shift == "km" ~
        magnitude_of_shift / n_years_midyear,
      
      # already km/year
      gradient == "horizontal" & unit_of_shift == "km/year" ~
        magnitude_of_shift,
      
      
      # anything unexpected
      TRUE ~ NA_real_

    ),
    
    unit_of_shift = case_when(
      gradient == "elevation" ~ "m/year",
      gradient %in% c("latitude", "longitude", "horizontal") ~ "km/year",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
      )
    )

rt5_latlon <- rt5 %>%
  
  group_by(
    publication_id,
    taxonomic_unit_revised,
    position,
    across(measurement_type:number_of_censuses)
  ) %>%
  
  # keep groups containing both latitude and longitude
  filter(
    all(c("latitude", "longitude") %in% gradient)
  ) %>%
  
  ungroup()


rt5_latlon_wide <- rt5_latlon %>%
  
  select(
    -c(comment:recorder_name,
       azimuth_of_shift, 
       shift_tested:notes,
       lat_mean)
  ) %>%
  
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = gradient,
    values_from = magnitude_of_shift
  ) %>%
  
  mutate(
    magnitude_of_shift = sqrt(
      longitude^2 + latitude^2
    ),
    
    azimuth_of_shift = (
      atan2(longitude, latitude) * 180 / pi + 360
    ) %% 360,
    gradient = "horizontal",
    unit_of_shift = "km/year",
    comment = "magnitude and azimuth of the horizontal shift estimated by combining latitude and longitude shift observations"
  )



rt6 <- bind_rows(rt5,
                 rt5_latlon_wide %>% 
                   select(-latitude, -longitude))

final edit

Code 
rt7 <- rt6 %>% 
  mutate(
    
    # ---------------------------------------------- #
    # based on publication
    
    ecosystem = case_when(
      publication_id == "Sakiyama 2024" ~ "forest, alpine",
      publication_id == "Shimazaki et al. 2011" ~ "subalpine",
      publication_id == "Kizawa et al. 2022" ~ "subalpine",
      
      # keep original value otherwise
      TRUE ~ as.character(ecosystem)
    ),
    
    information_source = case_when(
      information_source == "governmental monitoring survey" ~ "scientific survey",
      
      information_source == "literature" ~ "literature and specimens",
      information_source == "literature and specimens" ~ "literature and specimens",
      
      publication_id == "Kawauchi et al. 2023" ~ "fishery statistics",
      publication_id == "Tu et al. 2015" ~ "fishery statistics",
      
      publication_id == "Higashiguchi et al. 2025" ~ "scientific survey",
      publication_id == "Kakehi et al. 2021" ~ "scientific survey",
      
      # keep original value otherwise
      TRUE ~ as.character(information_source)
    )
  )

export

Code 
# ------------ #
rt_reorg <- rt7 %>% 
  select(-taxonomic_unit) %>% 
  # bring early
  relocate(include,
           geographic_scale:shift_source) %>% 
  # bring middle
  relocate(reference_no,
           publication_id:data_section,
           .after = language) %>% 
  # bring later
  relocate(comment, edit_info, recorder_name,
           .after = last_col()) %>% 
  arrange(publication_id,
          gradient, 
          position,
          kingdom,
          phylum,
          class,
          order,
          family,
          genus)

# check any issues in key columns

keycols <- c("taxonomic_unit_revised",
             "kingdom",
             "ecosystem",
             "realm",
             "gradient",
             "position",
             "observation",
             "startperiod_startyear",
             "startperiod_midyear",
             "endperiod_endyear",
             "endperiod_midyear",
             "n_years",
             "number_of_censuses",
             "magnitude_of_shift",
             "unit_of_shift",
             "language",
             "publication_id")


# display cols that have na
rt_reorg %>%
  summarise(
    across(
      all_of(keycols),
      ~ sum(is.na(.x))
    )
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    everything(),
    names_to = "column",
    values_to = "n_na"
  ) %>%
  filter(n_na > 0)

Column: notes

 [1] NA                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
 [2] "the shift change was estimated from fig. 4 using webplotdigitzer (https://automeris.io/wpd/?v=5_2)"                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       
 [3] "while the study focuses on the korean waters, this study was included because it mainly focuses on open sea species from the surrounding seas of japan. range shift was estimated by extracting data from the plots. the measurement of fish data was biomass. the latitude represents biomass-weighted monthly mean latitudes."                                                                          
 [4] "centriod in deapth and temperature gradient were also provided. length of the latitudinal shift was read from the figure showing 16 years regression line (trend analysis). caution is needed since this trend analyses ignores time autocorrelation (e.g., correlation between latitude centroid and calender year)."                                                                                    
 [5] "longitudinal shift was read from the figure showing 16 years regression line (trend analysis) by hayashi."                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                
 [6] "changes in the leading edge can be visually inferred from the maps of japan in figures 1 and 3; however, these estimates are imprecise because latitude, longitude, and the coordinate system are not provided. quantitatively, the results section only indicates the post-shift latitude as \"approximately 36°n\" and the discussion states that \"the range shifted northward from 33°n to 36°n\"."
 [7] "estimated from fig. 6b and taken as slope of linear regression on lat and lon of predicted cog. the significance correspond to that of the slope coefficient of the linear regression (significant if p-value <= 0.05)"                                                                                                                                                                                   
 [8] "fig 3 was used for extracting the latitude and year information and then linear regression was used to compute the significance of the shift."                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            
 [9] "森林限界のシフトを調査。"                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
[10] "number of censuses refer to total number of occurrences used for calculating the shifts (both coasts and all years)"                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
[11] "shifts calculated as least coast path distances along the coast between reported northernmost records between periods"                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    
[12] "the shift was stated in fig. 5 and esm4 for each species showing long term trend value."                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
[13] "tentative values used for magnitude, so change after receiving results"                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
[14] "resurvey of the past elevational plots"                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
[15] "na"                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       
[16] "shifts estimated from fig. 3. the significance tested corresponds to the overall centroid shift not the lat/lon ones as stated in the paper. azimuths (bearings) calculated from the lat/lon shifts."                                                                                                                                                                                                     
[17] "shifts estimated as the slope coefficient of the linear regression fitted to the annual lat and lon of centroids provided in sup. table s1. the significance test corresponds to the p-value of the regression slope (significant if p-value <= 0.05). azimuths (bearings) calculated from the initial and final coordinates of the centroid in the series."                                              
[18] "the shift represents change in abundance-weighted mean elevation calculated based on values shown in table 1. values for elevation 1300-1700m were used. significance testing was not conducted because it is not possible with this type of data sampling."                                                                                                                                              
[19] "shifts provided as minimum estimates of expansion rates over the period"                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
[20] "this change represents the change in average latitude calculated based on the mesh map shown in table 3."

 [6] "removed \"north\" in the azimuth column and kept it \"empty\" because the gradient is \"latitude\" for this data, not horizontal. edited the shiftsource column from \"no\" to \"estimated\" because dai estimated the magnitude of shift and its significance by extracting data."                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            
 [7] "na"                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            
 [8] "edited the entry for magnitude after recalculation. shift was computable for both latitude and longitude so the row was duplicated. the shift was calculated using the latitude and longitude coordinates of the cities based on table 1 and figure 1, of which the error is marginal considering thelarge extent of the study (western japan was the study area and sampling locations were indicated by city names). information on number of censuses was not provided in the literature. we assigned 39 for this column to present the number of studies that this e2247 study referred to build the species distribution records, based on the table 1, considering that one set of distribution survey (census) was conducted per study."
 [9] "magnitudeofshift, unitofshift, and shiftsource columns were recalculated after confirming with takahashi-san."                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
[10] "edited data entry for position from \"average (population density weighted)\" to \"centroid\". the study notes that population density weighted average will likely shift under warming but also that this average is not the same meaning as \"center of species range\" that was used by brown 1984 and brown et al. 1995. but \"centroid\" was used because most studies align with this definition of centroid, not necessarily matching with center of species range. also, removed \"north\" in the azimuth column and kept it \"empty\" because the gradient is \"latitude\" for this data, not horizontal."                                                                                                                            
[11] "removed \"north\" in the azimuth column and kept it \"empty\" because the gradient is \"latitude\" for this data, not horizontal."                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             
[12] "data entry for position column was edited to centroid from average. this is because the study covers largely the entire elevational limit that abies mariesii is found in. the species is found from above 1000m and the study used aerial photographs that covers this lower limit to higher limit. so the position could be considered centroid in the elevational gradient. /// although remote sensing analysis not conducted in a census style like field resurveys, number of censuses was edited from 1 to 2 considering that the census was conducted on the start and end year."                                                                                                                                                      
[13] "changed the number of censuses of seriola spp. from 126 to 128 because the collecting period is 1894-2021 (128 years)."

Analyze

Absolute rate ~ axis, realm, position

Code 
# ============================================== #
# Prepare horizontal range-shift data

rt_temp <- rt_cleaned %>%
  
  # ---------------------------------------------- #
  # Keep latitudinal and longitudinal shifts
  
  filter(
    gradient %in% c("latitude", "longitude"),
    !is.na(magnitude_of_shift)
  ) %>%
  
  # ---------------------------------------------- #
  # Create variables for analysis
  
  mutate(
    
    # Absolute range-shift rate (km/year)
    shift_rate_abs = abs(magnitude_of_shift),
    
    # Direction of range shift
    shift_direction = case_when(
      magnitude_of_shift > 0 ~ "positive",
      magnitude_of_shift < 0 ~ "negative",
      magnitude_of_shift == 0 ~ "zero",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    
    # Make variables factors
    gradient = factor(
      gradient,
      levels = c("latitude", "longitude")
    ),
    
    realm = factor(
      realm,
      levels = c("terrestrial", "marine")
    ),
    
    position = factor(position),
    
    shift_direction = factor(
      shift_direction,
      levels = c("negative", "positive", "zero")
    ),
    
    publication_id = factor(publication_id),
    taxonomic_unit_revised = factor(taxonomic_unit_revised)
  )

# Check data

  count(gradient, shift_direction)

# ============================================== #
# Remove zero shifts for positive vs negative analysis

# Zero has no direction, so exclude it from the model testing
# positive vs negative shifts.

rt_temp_model <- rt_temp %>%
  filter(
    shift_direction != "zero",
    !is.na(shift_direction),
    !is.na(realm),
    !is.na(position),
    !is.na(publication_id),
    !is.na(taxonomic_unit_revised)
  ) %>%
  droplevels()


# ============================================== #
# Linear mixed-effects model

mod_horizontal <- lmer(
  
  shift_rate_abs ~
    gradient * shift_direction +
    realm +
    position +
    (1 | publication_id) +
    (1 | taxonomic_unit_revised),
  
  data = rt_temp_model
)

# ============================================== #
# Realm color palettes

realm_palette <- function(realm, n) {
  
  # generate 1.5x as many colors
  # generate more colors when n = 1
  n_full <- if (n == 1) {
    ceiling(n * 3)
  } else {
    ceiling(n * 1.5)
  }
  
  
  # ---------------------------------------------- #
  # create full palette
  
  if (realm == "Marine") {
    
    cols <- grDevices::hcl.colors(
      n_full,
      palette = "Blues 3"
    )
    
  } else if (realm == "Terrestrial") {
    
    cols <- grDevices::hcl.colors(
      n_full,
      palette = "YlOrRd"
    )
    
  } else {
    
    cols <- grDevices::hcl.colors(
      n_full,
      palette = "Dark 3"
    )
  }
  
  
  # ---------------------------------------------- #
  # extract n colors around the middle
  
  start <- floor((n_full - n) / 2) + 1
  end <- start + n - 1
  
  cols[start:end]
}


# example
marine_colors <- realm_palette(
  "Marine",
  5
)

terrestrial_colors <- realm_palette(
  "Terrestrial",

)

  group_by(realm) %>%

Code 
# ============================================== #
# class level

bar_class <- rt_countobs %>%
  count(
    realm,
    kingdom,
    class
  ) %>%
  group_by(realm) %>%
  arrange(kingdom, class, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(
    prop = n / sum(n),
    xmax = cumsum(prop),
    xmin = lag(xmax, default = 0)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()


# ============================================== #
# kingdom level

bar_kingdom <- bar_class %>%
  group_by(
    realm,
    kingdom
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    xmin = min(xmin),
    xmax = max(xmax),
    x = (xmin + xmax) / 2,
    .groups = "drop"
  )


# ============================================== #
# kingdom label positions

bar_kingdom_label <- bar_kingdom %>%
  mutate(
    prop = xmax - xmin
  )


# ============================================== #
# large kingdoms: label inside bar

bar_kingdom_label_large <- bar_kingdom_label %>%
  filter(
    prop >= 0.1
  )


# ============================================== #
# small kingdoms: label outside bar

bar_kingdom_label_small <- bar_kingdom_label %>%
  filter(
    prop < 0.1
  ) %>%
  group_by(realm) %>%
  arrange(x, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(
    label_id = row_number(),
    label_row = (label_id - 1) %% 2,
    
    # move labels at edges toward the center
    label_x = case_when(
      x < 0.1 ~ x + 0.08,
      x > 0.9 ~ x - 0.08,
      TRUE ~ x
    ),
    
    label_y = 1.62 + 0.18 * label_row
  ) %>%
  ungroup()



# ============================================== #
# kingdom boundaries within class bar

bar_kingdom_boundary <- bar_kingdom %>%
  group_by(realm) %>%
  arrange(xmin, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  filter(
    xmax < 1
  ) %>%
  transmute(
    realm,
    boundary = xmax
  ) %>%
  ungroup()


# ============================================== #
# class label positions

bar_class_label <- bar_class %>%
  mutate(
    x = (xmin + xmax) / 2
  )


# ============================================== #
# large classes: label inside bar

bar_class_label_large <- bar_class_label %>%
  filter(
    prop >= 0.1
  )


# ============================================== #
# small classes: labels outside bar

bar_class_label_small <- bar_class_label %>%
  filter(
    prop < 0.1
  ) %>%
  group_by(realm) %>%
  arrange(x, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(
    label_id = row_number(),
    
    # alternate between two rows
    label_row = (label_id - 1) %% 2,
    
    # spread labels horizontally
    label_x = seq(
      0.08,
      0.92,
      length.out = n()
    ),
    
    # stagger vertically
    label_y = -0.18 - 0.18 * label_row
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>% 
  mutate(
    # edit manually
    label_x = case_when(
      class == "Liliopsida" ~ 0.5,
      class == "Bivalvia" ~ 0.06,
      class == "Cephalopoda" ~ 0.14, 
      class == "Elasmobranchii" ~ 0.24, 
      class == "Holothuroidea" ~ 0.34, 
      class == "Malacostraca" ~ 0.54, 
      class == "Polyplacophora" ~ 0.6, 
      class == "Florideophyceae" ~ 0.86, 
      
      TRUE ~ label_x
    ),
    
    # edit manually
    label_y = case_when(
      class == "Holothuroidea" ~ -0.36, 
      class == "Malacostraca" ~ -0.36, 
      class == "Polyplacophora" ~ -0.18, 
      
      TRUE ~ label_y
    )
  )


# ============================================== #
# class colors

n_class <- bar_class %>%
  distinct(class) %>%
  nrow()

class_colors <- grDevices::hcl.colors(
  n_class,
  palette = "Pastel 1"
)

names(class_colors) <- sort(
  unique(bar_class$class)
)

# ============================================== #
# Gantt chart-like plot of study duration per observation
#
# Equal vertical height for:
#   1. each realm
#   2. each reference within each realm


rt_temp <- rt_cleaned %>%
  
  filter(
    !is.na(startperiod_startyear),
    !is.na(endperiod_endyear)
  ) %>%
  
  
  # ---------------------------------------------- #
  # First year represented by each publication
  
  group_by(realm, publication_id) %>%
  mutate(
    publication_start = min(
      startperiod_startyear,
      na.rm = TRUE
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  
  
  # ---------------------------------------------- #
  # Arrange publications and observations
  
  arrange(
    realm,
    publication_start,
    publication_id,
    startperiod_startyear,
    endperiod_endyear
  ) %>%
  
  
  # ---------------------------------------------- #
  # Publication factor follows arranged order
  
  mutate(
    publication_id = factor(
      publication_id,
      levels = unique(publication_id)
    )
  ) %>%
  
  
  # ============================================== #
  # Give each reference an equal-height band
  # within each realm
  
  group_by(realm) %>%
  mutate(
    
    # reference order within realm
    reference_order = match(
      publication_id,
      unique(publication_id)
    ),
    
    # number of references in realm
    n_ref_realm = n_distinct(publication_id)
    
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  
  
  # ---------------------------------------------- #
  # Give each observation a position within
  # its reference band
  
  group_by(realm, publication_id) %>%
  mutate(
    
    n_entry = n(),
    obs_order = row_number(),
    
    # center of this reference's band
    reference_center = (
      reference_order - 0.5
    ) / n_ref_realm,
    
    # total vertical height available
    # to this reference
    reference_height = 1 / n_ref_realm,
    
    # observation positions within reference band
    #
    # observations occupy 70% of the available
    # reference band (±35% around the center)
    obs_offset = if (n() == 1) {
      
      0
      
    } else {
      
      (
        (obs_order - 1) / (n_entry - 1) - 0.5
      ) * 0.7 * first(reference_height)
      
    },
    
    # final y position
    obs_y = reference_center + obs_offset
    
  ) %>%
  
  ungroup() %>%
  
  mutate(
    realm = factor(
      realm,
      levels = c("terrestrial", "marine"),
      labels = c("Terrestrial", "Marine")
    ),
    census_linetype = case_when(
      number_of_censuses == 2 ~ "2 censuses",
      TRUE ~ ">2 censuses"
    )
  )


# ============================================== #
# Reference labels
#
# Because each reference now has its own
# equal-height band, simply use reference_center
# as the label position.


publication_labels <- rt_temp %>%
  
  group_by(
    realm,
    publication_id
  ) %>%
  
  summarise(
    label_y = first(reference_center),
    n_entry = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  
  mutate(
    publication_label = as.character(publication_id),
    
    publication_label = case_when(
      
      # References containing "et al."
      stringr::str_detect(publication_label, " et al\\. ") ~
        stringr::str_replace(
          publication_label,
          "^(.*?) et al\\. (.*)$",
          "'\\1 '*italic('et al.')*' \\2'"
        ),
      
      # References without "et al."
      TRUE ~ paste0(
        "'",
        publication_label,
        "'"
      )
    ),
    
    # Add italic (n = x)
    publication_label = paste0(
      publication_label,
      "*' ('*italic(n == ",
      n_entry,
      ")*')'"
    )
  )


# ============================================== #
# Publication colors by realm
# remove lightest 50% of each palette

publication_colors_df <- rt_temp %>%
  distinct(
    realm,
    publication_id
  ) %>%
  group_by(realm) %>%
  arrange(publication_id, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(
    color = case_when(
      
      realm == "Marine" ~ {
        
        cols <- grDevices::hcl.colors(
          ceiling(n() / 0.65),
          palette = "Blues 3"
        )
        
        # keep darkest 50%
        cols[seq_len(n())]
      },
      
      realm == "Terrestrial" ~ {
        
        cols <- grDevices::hcl.colors(
          ceiling(n() / 0.65),
          palette = "YlOrRd"
        )
        
        # keep darkest 50%
        cols[seq_len(n())]
      },
      
      TRUE ~
        grDevices::hcl.colors(
          n(),
          palette = "Dark 3"
        )
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup()


publication_colors <- publication_colors_df$color
names(publication_colors) <- publication_colors_df$publication_id

# ============================================== #
# common plotting function

kingdom_colors <- c(
  "Animalia" = "#0072B2",
  "Plantae" = "#009E73",
  "Chromista" = "#D55E00"
)

kingdom_shapes <- c(
  "Animalia" = 16,
  "Plantae" = 17,
  "Chromista" = 15
)


make_shift_plot <- function(data, gradient_value, y_title, n_row) {
  
  d <- data %>%
  filter(
    gradient == gradient_value
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    kingdom = factor(
      kingdom,
      levels = c(
        "Chromista",
        "Plantae",
        "Animalia"
      )
    )
  ) %>%
  group_by(
    realm,
    gradient,
    kingdom
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    n_group = n()
  ) %>%
  ungroup()
  
  
  # groups with enough observations for violin
  d_violin <- d %>%
    filter(
      n_group > 5
    )
  
  
  ggplot(
    d,
    aes(
      x = kingdom,
      y = magnitude_of_shift
    )
  ) +
    
    # ---------------------------------------------- #
    # zero line
    
    geom_hline(
      yintercept = 0,
      color = "black",
      linewidth = 0.6
    ) +
    
    
    # ---------------------------------------------- #
    # violin only for groups with > 5 observations
    
    geom_violin(
      data = d_violin,
      aes(
        fill = kingdom,
        color = kingdom
      ),
      width = 1,
      alpha = 0.25,
      linewidth = 0.8,
      trim = FALSE
    ) +
    
    
    # ---------------------------------------------- #
    # show points for ALL observations
    
    geom_jitter(
      aes(
        shape = kingdom,
        color = kingdom
      ),
      width = 0.2,
      height = 0,
      size = 3,
      alpha = 0.8
    ) +
    
    
    # ============================================== #
    # scales
    
    scale_x_discrete(
      limits = function(x) {
        intersect(
          c(
            "Chromista",
            "Plantae",
            "Animalia"
          ),
          x
        )
      }
    ) +
    
    
    scale_shape_manual(
      values = kingdom_shapes
    ) +
    
    scale_color_manual(
      values = kingdom_colors
    ) +
    
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = kingdom_colors
    ) +
    
    
    # ============================================== #
    # facets
    
    facet_wrap(
      ~ realm,
      nrow = n_row
    ) +
    
    
    labs(
      x = NULL,
      y = y_title
    ) +
    
    
    theme_bw(base_size = 20) +
    
    theme(
      legend.position = "none",
      strip.background = element_rect(
        fill = "grey90"
      ),
      axis.text.x = element_text(
        angle = 20,
        hjust = 1
      )
    )
}

# marine
rt_horizontal_20ma <- rt_temp %>%
  filter(
    gradient == "Horizontal",
    realm == "Marine",
    !is.na(azimuth_of_shift),
    !is.na(magnitude_of_shift),
    magnitude_of_shift <= 20
  )


g_horizontal_circular_20ma <- ggplot(
  rt_horizontal_20ma,
  aes(
    x = azimuth_of_shift,
    y = magnitude_of_shift,
    color = kingdom,
    shape = kingdom
  )
) +
  
  # ---------------------------------------------- #
  # movement vector
  
  geom_segment(
    aes(
      xend = azimuth_of_shift,
      y = 0,
      yend = magnitude_of_shift
    ),
    linewidth = 0.5,
    alpha = 0.5
  ) +
  
  # ---------------------------------------------- #
  # endpoint
  
  geom_point(
    size = 3,
    alpha = 0.8
  ) +
  
  
  # ============================================== #
  # scales
  
  scale_x_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 360),
    breaks = c(
      0, 45, 90, 135,
      180, 225, 270, 315
    ),
    labels = c(
      "N", "NE", "E", "SE",
      "S", "SW", "W", "NW"
    ),
    expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 20),
    breaks = seq(0, 20, by = 5),
    expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  
  scale_shape_manual(
    values = kingdom_shapes
  ) +
  
  scale_color_manual(
    values = kingdom_colors
  ) +
  
  
  # ============================================== #
  # circular coordinates
  
  coord_polar(
    theta = "x",
    start = 0,
    direction = 1
  ) +
  
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = NULL
  ) +
  
  theme_bw(base_size = 20) +
  
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    
    plot.background = element_rect(
      color = "white",
      fill = "white",
      linewidth = 0.8
    ),
    
    plot.margin = margin(

    )
